heard: A billion light-year hole in space might be a cosmic bruise. In 2004, astronomers scanning the Big Bang's ancient afterglow found a massive, unexpected anomaly. NASA's WMAP satellite detected a distinct cold spot in the constellation Eridanus that shouldn't exist. This supervoid spans nearly two billion light-years and is almost entirely empty of all normal matter. Ancient light photons lose energy as they crossed this wasteland through the integrated Sachs-Wolf effect. The feature was so unexpected that some researchers nicknamed it the axis of evil. One mind-bending theory suggests this massive gap is where our universe collided with a parallel one. Such an ancient impact would leave a permanent scar.
